finding: A `review-open` refusal from a review that has already stopped can never clear, but the skill says to finish the review and mark again.
why: Failing inputs: (a) a subtask review stopped `unfixed`, or stopped `cap` with a finding that has no outcome, keeps `left.blocking` not empty, and `outcome` and `begin` then refuse `review-over`; (b) `open` made a new Draft after the old change closed, so `str(answer.get("change")) != change` holds for every finished review, and `begin` refuses for the same reason. `finish` repeats the same report in both cases, so the agent loops. `mark-ready` itself makes case (a) worse: its `finish` stamps `stopped_by` at the cap before the fixer records the outcome.
fix: Split the refusal: a stopped review with `left.blocking` or another change id routes to the developer, who decides or marks Ready; only a review that can still run says finish it. Give the row that next action, and add a test on the real review command for a stopped `unfixed` review.
evidence: SKILL.md: "| `review-open` | `reviews` names each subtask and why | finish that review, then mark again |". review_rounds.py:125-126 `if state["stopped_by"] is not None: raise Refusal("review-over", ...)`, called by `begin` (line 142) and `outcome` (line 296). ci_watch.py:262 `if str(answer.get("change")) != change:`. code-review/SKILL.md:48 "`review-over` | this subtask's review has stopped | `finish` repeats the report". Verified by reading; not run.

criterion: acceptance: at ship, with review settled and CI green, the agent marks the change Ready (PRD AC-064)
finding: "Review settled" is not bound to the commits on the change, so a commit pushed after the reviews stopped reaches Ready with no review.
why: The skill's own `ci-red` action is "fix and push", but `finish` only repeats the stored report and `begin` refuses a stopped review, so the fix commit (or a target merge with resolved conflicts) can never be reviewed and `_why_open` still answers settled; D-46 defines settled but does not name this case.
fix: Have the gate compare the commit the review last read with the change head and refuse on later commits, or record in the ledger that commits after the reviews are accepted unreviewed; at minimum run the read-only head and CI checks before `finish`.
evidence: ci_watch.py `_why_open` reads only `left.blocking`, `left.not_posted`, `change`, `stopped_by`, and no commit. review_rounds.py:142 `_refuse_unless_running(state)` in `begin`, :126 `the review of ... stopped`, :353 `if state["stopped_by"] is None:` in `finish`. SKILL.md:70 `fix and push`. ci_watch.py:284 runs `_open_reviews` before the head and CI reads, and the test asserts `ship["forge"].calls == []` on that order. D-46: "Cost: `finish` at ship stops a review that owes no more work".

criterion: acceptance: at ship, with review settled and CI green, the agent marks the change Ready (PRD AC-064)
finding: The ship flow marks straight after a push, and an empty CI read then hands Ready to the developer as "the change has no checks" when the checks may not be registered yet.
why: Ship step 1 runs the push and step 2 marks at once; `ci-status` is one read, while the port's `ci-wait` treats an empty status as not yet a verdict and reads 3 times, so a change with real CI can be routed to a human and the agent does not mark it Ready.
fix: On an empty status right after a push, have `mark-ready` or the skill wait through `watch` first, and keep `ci-none` for the case where `watch` also ends with no status.
evidence: SKILL.md:62 `Run "Open or update the change" with the final proofs` (its step 1 is `Push`), SKILL.md:71 `ci-none | the change has no checks | report it; the developer marks the change Ready`. ci_watch.py:293 one `forge_answer("ci-status", ...)`. common.py:98 `gave no status: auth, network, or no checks on the change; not a verdict`. Unverified: how long a real forge shows no checks after a push; not measured here.

criterion: acceptance: CI watch runs in the background after each push and reports the result (PRD AC-065)
finding: A broken watch record makes `start` refuse for good, and the refusal's only remedy is to run `start` again.
why: `start_watch` reads the old record for `previous` before it writes a new one, with no catch, so after one unreadable record no background watch can start on that change until someone deletes the file; the test covers `status` only.
fix: In `start_watch`, catch the `bad-record` refusal, report it in `previous` and write the new record; add a test for `start` on a broken record.
evidence: ci_watch.py:171 `previous = _report(change, _read_record(path))`; `_read_record` raises `Refusal("bad-record", f"the watch record {path} is unreadable: {error}; run `start`")`. SKILL.md: `bad-record ... reason names the fix`. Only test: `test_status_reads_a_broken_record_as_a_refusal` calls `status`. Found by reading; not run.

criterion: decision ledger D-48 carried into the skill
finding: D-48 says the developer starts a manual job, but the skill never routes to the developer, so a job that waits for a human loops on `watch` and `mark-ready`.
why: A manual job reads `running`; the `ci-running` row says to run `watch` and mark again, `watch` ends after its budget with `no-verdict`, the `no-verdict` row says to read CI at ship, and the next `mark-ready` answers `ci-running` again, with no step that tells a human.
fix: In the `ci-running` row, add: when `watch` ends with `no-verdict` and status `running`, report to the developer that a check may wait for a human, and stop.
evidence: D-48: "A manual job reads `running`, and the port has no verb to start one, so the developer starts it". CONTRACT.md: "a pipeline or check that waits for a human (GitLab `manual`, GitHub `ACTION_REQUIRED`), reads `running`". SKILL.md:69 `checks still run, or wait for a human | run `watch` ... its exit wakes you, then mark again`. SKILL.md:52 `no-verdict ... `start` after the next push, or read CI at ship`.

finding: The background-start test gives its child no budget and its fixture has no teardown, so a failure leaves a stray process and the regression it guards hangs instead of failing.
why: The child polls with the default 5400 s budget until the release file exists, and the test writes that file only after its asserts: a failed assert leaves a process polling each second for 90 minutes, and a `start` that blocks on the child never reaches the `< 20` assert until the budget ends (no pytest-timeout in the repository).
fix: Pass a small `budget` such as 60 to `start`, and write the release file after the `yield` in `child_forge`.
evidence: Line 463 `run(ci_watch, capsys, "start", id="7", forge="github", interval=1)`; line 449 `yield release` is the end of the fixture; ci_watch.py `DEFAULT_BUDGET = 5400`; `git grep -i pytest-timeout` over toml, ini, cfg, lock and txt files has no hit.

finding: No default-run test proves the watch outlives the process that ran `start`.
why: `run` calls `main` in the pytest process, which stays alive for the whole test, but the skill runs `start` as a short command that exits; PRD AC-065 background behaviour depends on the child surviving that exit, and only the `@live` test, skipped by default, starts it from a process that exits.
fix: Run `start` through `subprocess.run` with the JSON on stdin, as `_real` does, and let that process exit before the release file is written.
evidence: Line 84 `code = module.main([verb, json.dumps(payload)])`; SKILL.md "with one JSON object on stdin"; `_real` is used only under `@live` (`live = pytest.mark.skipif(not LIVE, ...)`, test line 733).

finding: `child_forge` writes only `gh.cmd`, so the background-start test works on Windows only.
why: `shell.run_tool` finds the tool with `shutil.which("gh")`, which on POSIX does not find `gh.cmd`, so the child answers `unavailable` or calls a real gh, the record reaches `no-verdict`, and `wait_for(... == "finished")` fails after 30 s; the sibling test file already has the POSIX branch.
fix: Copy the `os.name == "nt"` branch with the executable `#!/bin/sh` launcher from `test_code_review.py`, or share one helper.
evidence: Line 447 `(tools / "gh.cmd").write_text(...)`; test_code_review.py:450-455 `if os.name == "nt": ... else: launcher = stubs / "gh" ... launcher.chmod(0o755)`. POSIX result is inferred by reading, not run. `.github/workflows/tests.yml` has an ubuntu row but runs only `pytest scripts/tests`, so CI does not show this today.

finding: The multi-slice watch loop is proved only by its read count: the heartbeat, the slice budget and the read time limit have no assert.
why: The fake discards `limit` and no test reads `beat_at` after a slice, so 2 regressions pass: dropping `wait + READ_MARGIN` (a 600 s slice under the 300 s default limit ends each real watch as `no-verdict`), and dropping the beat write (`status` reports a live watch as `lost` after 1800 s). Survival is by reading; no mutation was run.
fix: Record `limit` in `Forge.__call__`, assert the `budget` and `limit` of each `ci-wait` call, and assert that `beat_at` advanced on the record after a `running` answer, plus a `status` test just under `LOST_AFTER`.
evidence: Line 63 `def __call__(self, verb, payload, limit=None):` never uses `limit`; line 338 `forge.verbs().count("ci-wait") == 3` is the only loop assert; ci_watch.py `call_forge("ci-wait", {...}, wait + READ_MARGIN)` and `_write_record(path, {**record, "beat_at": time.time()})`; the only `beat_at` in the test file is line 402, which sets it back.

finding: The gate's reading of `left.blocking` and `left.not_posted` is tested only against a hand-written report; the one real-command test records no findings.
why: `_why_open` uses `left.get(key)`, so it fails open: if `review_rounds.py` renames either key, the `SETTLED` fakes still pass and the real-command test still passes because its lists are empty, and Ready then goes through with open findings.

Today the keys match `_report` in review_rounds.py (`left={"blocking": ..., "posted": ..., "not_posted": ...}`).

finding: The failure branches of `_call` have no test: no answer, non-JSON output, a timeout, and an answer with no `ok`.
why: Every gate and open test replaces `call_forge` or `call_review`, and the real-process tests only pass through the success path, so the rule that a crashed or hung port or review command becomes a refusal rests on no test, although the Ready gate relies on it.

finding: A `git fetch` that runs past its limit makes `merge-facts` refuse `timeout` and never answers `fetched: false`.
why: Failing input: a slow or hanging remote for more than 120 s. `shell.run_tool` raises `Refusal("timeout")` on TimeoutExpired, and it also raises when the start of git fails, so the `returncode == 0` test is not reached. The skill promises that a failed fetch gives facts from the last fetch, and those local facts are available. The fetch-failure test covers only a nonzero exit.

finding: `mark-ready` runs the review's `finish`, which cannot be undone, before the checks that can refuse.
why: A call with the wrong `id`, a merged change, `head-differs` or `ci-red` still stops each review and posts what is left, and after a `ci-red` the skill says fix and push while `begin` then refuses `review-over`, so that fix has no review route.

D-46 accepts the stop as a cost ("finish at ship stops a review that owes no more work") but does not decide this order.

finding: The Ready gate claims green CI on the head, but the CI answer it reads names no commit.
why: `ci-status` answers only `status` and `url`, and GitLab reads `head_pipeline.status` with no compare to `sha`, so a read just after a push can show the previous pipeline's result, or no checks on GitHub, which routes to `ci-none` and hands the change to the developer.

finding: Possible Windows flake: the 50 ms poll reads the record file while the child replaces it.
why: On Windows `os.replace` over a file that another process holds open raises `PermissionError`, and a reader can get the same error during the replace; neither `record_of` nor `_write_record` catches it, so the test can raise, or the child can lose its final result and the wait runs out.

finding: The gate and the watch record compare the change id as literal text, so one change given in 2 forms reads as 2 changes.
why: Failing input: review `begin` with change `7`, then `mark-ready` with `id` `https://f.test/a/pull/7`; the refusal is `the review posted on change 7, not https://...` although it is the same change. In the same way, `start` with the number and `status` with the url read 2 record files, so `status` answers `none`. The test test_a_change_url_gets_one_record_file shows a url is an accepted id.
fix: Normalize `id` once through `change-view` before the compare in `mark_ready_if_green`, or refuse a non-number id, and document the one accepted form.
evidence: ci_watch.py:262 `if str(answer.get("change")) != change:`; ci_watch.py:113 `return Path(folder) / "afkv2-ci" / f"{_NOT_A_FILE_NAME.sub('_', change)}.json"`. Fails safe at the gate.

finding: The Draft read-back runs only in the create path, so a retry of `open` answers ok on a change that is not Draft.
why: Failing input: `_create` writes the change and its read-back `change-view` times out, or it refuses `not-draft`. The next `open` finds the change through `_existing`, takes the update path, and answers `ok` with `created: false, draft: false`. Skill step 4 says "Done when the answer holds `id`", so an agent that retries goes on with a change open for review. The people given to a create that failed after the write are lost the same way: `open` never sets them on an existing change (gh behaviour on such a failure is unverified).
fix: Refuse `not-draft` in the update path when the description is written for the first time, or make step 4 say that `draft: false` before ship must be reported.
evidence: change_request.py:129 `return ok(id=view["id"], url=view.get("url") or "", draft=bool(view.get("draft")), created=False)`; change_request.py:117-118 is the only `not-draft` check. DECISIONS.md D-51: "the read-back is the only proof of AC-064 'opens as Draft'".

finding: The takeover check and the write are 2 steps, so an older watch can overwrite the record of a `start` that lands between them.
why: Failing order: the older watch passes `_is_current` in `_end` (line 204) or `watch_ci` (line 234), `start` writes its new token, then the older watch writes its record with the old token. The new child then reads itself as superseded and stops, and the new commit gets no watch: at `_end`, `status` shows `finished` for the older head and never `lost`. The window is narrow, and D-47 states "the older process ... writes nothing". The same check reads a transient read error as superseded, because `_is_current` turns `bad-record` into False.
fix: Accept and record the narrow window in D-47, or guard the write with a per-change lock file; let `_is_current` retry once on a read error.
evidence: ci_watch.py:204 `if not _is_current(path, record["token"]):` then ci_watch.py:207 `_write_record(path, final)`; ci_watch.py:242 `_write_record(path, {**record, "beat_at": time.time()})`. Found by reading; the race was not reproduced.

finding: `mark-ready` does not pass `forge` and `repo` to the review's `finish`, although the skill says every payload's values reach the forge port.
why: Failing input: `mark-ready` with `forge` or `repo` set, on a clone where the config and `origin` do not give the same answer. `finish` retries its unposted findings with auto-detection (`_comment_payload` holds only `id` and `text`): they fail `no-forge` and stay `not_posted`, which holds `review-open`, or they go to the repository of `origin`. The review script has no input for these values and is outside this slice's Scope.
fix: Narrow the sentence on SKILL.md line 20 to the forge calls of these 2 scripts and name the review's posts as auto-detected, or add the values to the review command in a slice that owns it.
evidence: ci_watch.py:53 `return _call(REVIEW, "finish", {"plan": str(plan), "subtask": subtask}, REVIEW_LIMIT)`. SKILL.md:20 "Every payload can hold `forge` and `repo`, and the scripts pass them to the forge port." review_rounds.py:230 `payload = {"id": state["change"], "text": _comment_text(entry)}`.

finding: Possible misuse: `open` on an existing change drops `target` with no message.
why: `merge-facts` and the mergeability case can rest on one target while the open change targets another, and `open` answers ok, so the description makes a false merge claim.
fix: When the payload holds `target`, compare it with `view["target"]` and refuse a difference.
evidence: change_request.py:128 `forge_answer("change-update-body", payload, id=view["id"], body=body)`; CONTRACT.md `change-view` answers `target`; SKILL.md:40 names only "The title, the assignee and the reviewers are set only when the change is created"; D-49 does not name the target.

finding: Possible drift: the new code `command-failed` is in no table, and it repeats `cli-failed` and `forge-failed`.
why: SKILL.md sends any other code to the forge port contract, whose table does not hold `command-failed`, so the reader gets no next action for it.
fix: Add `command-failed` to the SKILL.md refusal table with its next action, or use the port's `cli-failed`.
evidence: ci_watch.py:41 `envelope.fail("command-failed", ...)`; SKILL.md:77 "other codes | the forge port's error codes, with its `reason` | `afkv2/ports/forge/CONTRACT.md`"; tracker/CONTRACT.md:47 Transport "`network`, `timeout`, `bad-answer`, `cli-failed`, `internal`"; review_rounds.py:48 `forge-failed`. Search for `command-failed|forge-failed|cli-failed` under afkv2 gave only these sites and the shell and its tests.

finding: Possible gap: the skill does not document `budget` and `interval`, the state `superseded`, or `clean`, `ahead` and `behind`.
why: The forge port's contract lists each payload and answer field per verb, but this skill does not, so a caller of `watch` does not know the limit of the wait or what `superseded` means.
fix: Add one verb table to SKILL.md with the payload and answer fields of each verb, and mark `token` as internal to `start`.
evidence: ci_watch.py:169 `_seconds(payload, "budget", DEFAULT_BUDGET), _seconds(payload, "interval", None)`; ci_watch.py:193 `state="superseded"`; change_request.py:153 `clean=..., ahead=..., behind=...`. Search for `token`, `budget|interval|superseded|clean|ahead` in SKILL.md gave no line.

finding: Possible needless field: `start` answers `record`, the file path, and no reader uses it.
why: SKILL.md routes every read through `status` and calls the record the watch's own, so the path invites a direct read of a file whose shape nothing promises.
fix: Remove `record` from the answer of `start`.
evidence: ci_watch.py:181 `return ok(id=change, state="watching", record=str(path), previous=previous)`; SKILL.md:46 "The watch writes its result to a record; `status` makes no forge call." Search for `["record"]` and `.get("record")` in test_change_request.py gave no line; 0015 names no such field.
